prompts.system_prompt:
Your task is to write research paper on developing a new variational method for quantum many body physics and rebuttal againsit the referrees.
When writing LaTeX, you must: - Use \be for \begin{equation} and \ee for \end{equation}. - Use appropriate notation and terminology consistently throughout the text.
prompts.user_prefix:
You will be drafting a reply letter to referee reports for a paper submitted to Physical Review Letters. Here are the inputs you will need:
<documents> <document index="1"> <source>Cover Letter</source> <document_content> {COVER_LETTER} </document_content> </document> <document index="2"> <source>{INPUT_FILE}</source> <document_content> {MAIN_CONTENT} </document_content> </document> <document index="3"> <source>Appendix</source> <document_content> {SUPP_CONTENT} </document_content> </document> <document index="4"> <source>Editor Decision Letter</source> <document_content> {EDITOR_DECISION_LETTER} </document_content> </document> <document index="5"> <source>Referee Report A</source> <document_content> {REFEREE_REPORT_A} </document_content> </document> <document index="6"> <source>Referee Report B</source> <document_content> {REFEREE_REPORT_B} </document_content> </document> <document index="7"> <source>Example Reply Letter</source> <document_content> {EXAMPLE_REPLY_LETTER} </document_content> </document> <document index="8"> <source>Instructions</source> <document_content> {INSTRUCTION} </document_content> </document> </documents>
Explanation of documents: 1. Cover Letter: The original cover letter submitted with the paper. 2. Main Paper: The full text of the submitted paper, identified by {INPUT_FILE}. 3. Appendix: Supplementary information for the paper. 4. Editor Decision Letter: The full text of the editor's decision and comments. 5. Referee Report A: The full text of the first referee's report. 6. Referee Report B: The full text of the second referee's report. 7. Example Reply Letter: A sample reply letter for reference. 8. Instructions: Guidelines on how to draft the reply letter.
prompts.user_request:
Please read the paper, referee reports, and example reply carefully. Then, before drafting your full reply, write out your plan inside <scratchpad></scratchpad> tag. Consider which comments from the referee you agree with and will address with changes, and which you will rebut and argue against changing. Refer to the example reply for guidance on tone and structure.
After your planning, draft a reply letter that includes the following: 1. A 1-page cover letter to the editor. Summarize the key comments you will make in your reply. Write this inside the <cover_letter></cover_letter> tag. 2. A point-by-point response to the referee comments. To do this: - Split each referee report in the <referee_report_a></referee_report_a> or <referee_report_b></referee_report_b> tag into individual segment. Copy each exact comments as verbatim segment within the <referee_comment></referee_comment> tag. - Similar to the provided example, all the referee's comments (summary, recommendtions, criticisms, questions) need to be covered covered and addressed in the <point_by_point_reply_a></point_by_point_reply_a> or <point_by_point_reply_b></point_by_point_reply_b> tag. For recommendtions by the referee, we thank the referee politely and use it as an opportunity to amplify our main points. For criticisms, we also thank the referee, but address the criticisms firmly and be specific about what are changed in the paper, similar to the provided example. - Write your rebuttal to each comment inside the <author_response></author_response> tag immediately after each <referee_comment></referee_comment>. Be respectful and diplomatic, but firm in your responses. Follow the principles from the book "They Say, I Say" in crafting your rebuttals. Use "Show, not tell" approach - be specific about what are changed in the paper, similar to the provided example. 3. At the end of each reply to the referers, write a concluding paragraph to further persuade the referee. At the end of the reply letter, write a list of major changes you made to the paper. 4. A revised version of the paper that addresses the referee comments and implement all the proposed changes mentioned in the reply letter. Include the full text of the revised paper inside the <revised_paper></revised_paper> tag.
Write the full reply letter in the following format:
<reply_letter> <cover_letter> Your 1-page cover letter to the editor here. </cover_letter>
Responses to Referee A: <point_by_point_reply_a> <referee_comment> First comment from the referee A here. Potentially it is a summary of our work. </referee_comment> <author_response> Your rebuttal to the first comment here. </author_response>
<referee_comment> Second comment from the referee A here. </referee_comment> <author_response> Your rebuttal to the second comment here. </author_response>
(Continue this pattern for each comment from the referee.)
</point_by_point_reply_a>
Responses to Referee B: <point_by_point_reply_b> ... </point_by_point_reply_b>
<list_of_major_changes> List of major changes you made to the paper. Order by importance. Minor improvements to the presentation of the paper can be grouped into one item. </list_of_major_changes>
</reply_letter>
<revised_paper> Full text of your revised paper here. </revised_paper>
Remember, the goal is to be respectful and appreciative of the referee's efforts, while still advocating firmly and persuasively for your work and only making changes you agree are necessary. Start with laying down your plan in the <scratchpad></scratchpad> tag. Then proceed to drafting the reply letter in the the <reply_letter></reply_letter> tag.
prompts.user_reflect:
Your output (cover letter to the editor and the response letter to the referees) is too generic and not specific enough. After thoroughly and critically reviewing the paper, the cover letters, the report, the reply letter, and the example, write a new reply letter that satisfies the following requirements: <requirements> - Increases the level of details from moderate (6/10) to high (9/10), with specific references to the changes in the new version of the paper. - Make sure all the referee's comments (whether summary, recommendations, criticisms, or questions) have been addressed using concrete and convincing physical arguement. - The style and tone of the reply letter should be similar to the provided example (under <example_reply_letter>). </requirements>
Please output the revised cover letter (under <cover_letter>) and the revised response letter (under <point_by_point_reply_a> and <point_by_point_reply_b>) that meets the above requirements.
